name: The Grange (Wyoming Farm complex)
history: Surviving part of Frederick Augustus Hely's Wyoming Farm complex. Heritage NSW identifies it as a John Verge-designed homestead/stables complex built using assigned convict labour.

name: Henry Kendall Cottage / Cooranbean / Red Cow Inn
history: Early stone cottage associated with Peter Fagan. It later became closely associated with poet Henry Kendall. The site is also important as an early inn/farm/social stopping place.

name: Mulholland's Farm
history: Part of an early 640-acre Crown grant. The surviving farm is significant as an intact Brisbane Water farm from the later subdivision/farming era.

name: Alison Homestead
yearLabel: First land grant on site dates to 1825; Alison family from 1875
history: Museum site on land described by Alison Homestead as Wyong's first land grant, dating to 1825. The Alison family acquired the property in 1875 and developed the homestead and farming enterprise.

name: Pioneer Park
yearLabel: Historic cemetery landscape; exact first-use date to verify
history: Historic cemetery/public landscape at Point Frederick. It is now one of Central Coast Council's listed historic cemetery places. Earlier burial-ground references should be traced through newspapers and gazettes.

name: Noraville Cemetery
history: One of the oldest continuing public burial grounds on the northern Central Coast. Council states it opened in 1869.

name: St Barnabas Cemetery
yearLabel: Opened 1885 (Council history; exact coordinate to refine)
history: Historic Yarramalong Valley cemetery at 1671 Yarramalong Road. Useful for tracing early valley families and community gathering around the church/cemetery.

name: Yarramalong Cemetery
history: Council records this general cemetery as opening in 1888. It preserves the history of early Yarramalong families.

name: Jilliby Cemetery
history: Council records the cemetery as opening in 1896. It is another surviving marker of the northern district's early rural communities.

name: Wyong Racecourse / Picnic Races
yearLabel: Picnic races documented in Trove, 14 June 1923
confidence: Present racecourse vicinity; historic footprint to verify
history: The Gosford Times and Wyong District Advocate advertised the Wyong Picnic Races in June 1923, including train access for visitors. This is a strong documented mass-gathering location.

name: Terrigal Market Day & District Show – E. Wilson's Picture Hall
confidence: Terrigal town-centre approximation; hall site needs research
history: Trove records a successful Market Day and District Show held in E. Wilson's Picture Hall. The exact hall location is a research target.

name: Ourimbah Queen of the Day – New Hall
confidence: Ourimbah town-centre approximation; hall site needs research
history: The Gosford Times reported the crowning of the Ourimbah Queen of the Day in the new hall before a very large gathering.

name: Woy Woy – holiday excursion centre
yearLabel: Large Christmas holiday crowds documented in 1927
history: The Sydney Morning Herald reported large Christmas holiday crowds at Woy Woy in 1927 and described it as the railway centre for Brisbane Water. This represents the wider rail, ferry, fishing and holiday precinct rather than one single lot.

sources.label: Trove – Christmas at Woy Woy, 29 Dec 1927

name: Ocean Beach / Umina recreation reserve
yearLabel: Cricket-pitch request documented 1936; earlier holiday use to research
history: Ocean Beach was already functioning as a major recreation/holiday area by the interwar period. In 1936 the Ocean Beach Progress Association asked Woy Woy Shire Council to provide a cricket pitch on the oval.

name: Warrah Reserve
history: Historic protected landscape above Patonga and Pearl Beach. It is important to the Coast's early conservation history and also sits within an older walking, lookout and excursion landscape.

name: The Entrance – holiday, fishing & bathing precinct
yearLabel: Interwar holiday-resort era; individual sites to be dated
history: The Entrance developed as a major holiday centre around the channel, beaches and Tuggerah Lakes. This marker is a research hub for historic bathing, fishing, camping, amusement and excursion sites.

name: Waterview Park
yearLabel: Park/reserve shown in early Gosford mapping context; naming date to verify
history: A long-standing Gosford open-space landscape. Early Gosford maps show substantial public reserve/park areas; the exact sequence leading to the modern Waterview Park name remains a gazette/Trove research task.
